validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification; row is real and correctly classified
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: Rover Pipeline is extensively, independently documented (FERC dockets CP15-93/94/96, PGJ, OGJ, Daily Energy Insider, Reuters, Wikipedia, SEC filings) as a 711-713 mile, 3.25 Bcf/d (later 3.425 Bcf/d) interstate gas transmission line from the Marcellus/Utica shale (WV/OH/PA) to Michigan and the Union Gas Dawn Hub in Ontario, operated by Energy Transfer. GEM records the system as 4 rows: P0392 'Phase 1' (711 mi, 1700 MMcf/d, in service Dec 2017), P2438 'Phase 2' (this row, 0 new mi, 1550 MMcf/d, full completion 2018), P2604 'Rover Expansion' (0 mi, 175 MMcf/d, 2020), P2635 'Wick Meter Station Expansion' (0 mi, 300 MMcf/d, WV->WV). Capacity arithmetic checks out at every step: 1700 (Phase 1, confirmed Dec 2017 by dailyenergyinsider.com and ogj.com) + 1550 (Phase 2) = 3250 = the 3.25 Bcf/d design capacity independently confirmed by dailyenergyinsider.com, ogj.com, pgjonline.com and the Feb 2015 FERC filing (govinfo.gov Federal Register notice) for the full project; +175 (P2604) = 3.425 Bcf/d, independently confirmed as Rover's current total capacity by boereport.com's April 2026 Ares/Blackstone reporting. NOT A DUPLICATE: Phase 1 and Phase 2 are additive halves of one project completed in stages (Phase 1 = mainline to 1.7 Bcf/d by Dec 2017; Phase 2 = the remaining compression/facilities -- Mainline Compressor Stations 2 and 3 in Wayne/Crawford County, OH, plus the Sherwood/CGT laterals in WV -- that brought the system to its full 3.25 Bcf/d design capacity by Nov 2018), not a relabel or segment double-count of P0392. LENGTH/DIAMETER: LengthKnown=0/Diameter blank is CORRECT per the SOP's expansion-with-no-new-physical-pipe convention -- dailyenergyinsider.com and ogj.com both describe Phase 2's discrete facilities as compressor stations and a short interconnecting stretch of line already within the total mileage attributed to Phase 1's 711-713 mi (consistently reported as the WHOLE project's length across every source checked, including the original Feb 2015 FERC filing); confirmed, not fixed. LOCATION: StartState=Ohio/EndState=Michigan is directionally correct -- Phase 2's facilities (MCS2 Wayne Co OH, MCS3 Crawford Co OH) sit on the Ohio->Michigan leg of the system, and Rover's own pipe terminates at Michigan interconnects (e.g. Vector Pipeline) rather than crossing into Ontario itself (gas continues to the Dawn Hub via other pipelines), so EndCountryOrArea=United States is also correct. Opened dailyenergyinsider.com, ogj.com, pgjonline.com (x2 articles), worldpipelines.com (FAIL on url_verifier's '3.25' substring screen but hand-read and consistent), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rover_pipeline, the Feb 2015 FERC Federal Register filing notice (govinfo.gov, read via pdftotext), naturalgasintel.com's original FERC-filing article, boereport.com + blackstone.com + pgjonline.com's April 2026 Ares acquisition coverage, and gem.wiki (leads only, never cited) -- 10 of the row's 14 harvested wiki citations were opened; the 4 not reopened (Rextag paywall listing, Livingston Daily/MLive/Grist/DeSmog local-opposition stories, PBS spill story) were skipped as immaterial to the data-point audit (protest/incident coverage, not spec/attribution).

validity.recommendation: update Owner2 from 'Blackstone' to 'Ares Management' (32.4% stake); Owner1 (Energy Transfer, operator) and Owner3 (Traverse) are unaffected and remain accurate
validity.researcher_notes: The current Owner2='Blackstone' (32.44%) is STALE. On April 29, 2026, Ares Management (via its Infrastructure Opportunities strategy) acquired the entire 32.4% stake in Rover Pipeline from Blackstone Energy Transition Partners -- confirmed independently by Blackstone's own press release (blackstone.com), Pipeline & Gas Journal (pgjonline.com), and BOE Report (boereport.com), all dated late April 2026 and all naming both 'Rover Pipeline' and the 32.4% figure (matching GEM's 32.44%). Additional independent secondary confirmation via gurufocus.com and Seeking Alpha/Reuters (not individually re-verified through url_verifier, but consistent). This ownership change applies to ALL FOUR Rover Pipeline rows (P0392, P2438, P2604, P2635), not just Phase 2 -- see cross_row_leads. Owner1 (Energy Transfer, 32.57%, operator) and Owner3 (Traverse Midstream, 35.00%) are not implicated by this transaction and should be left as-is pending independent confirmation of their current percentages.

validity.recommendation: seek a primary source (FERC cost estimate specific to Phase 2 facilities, or a 10-K capitalized-cost breakdown) before treating SegmentCost=$1,220,000,000 as independently verified at the segment level
validity.researcher_notes: SegmentCost=$1,220,000,000 USD is arithmetically consistent with the independently-confirmed $4.22 billion total project cost (govinfo.gov Feb 2015 FERC Federal Register filing, states 'estimates the cost of the Rover Project to be approximately $4.22 [billion]'; also naturalgasintel.com's original FERC-filing article) minus Phase 1's reported $3 billion (per gem.wiki's own infobox -- not independently corroborated as a distinct Phase 1 figure either). I could not find a primary source stating $1.22 billion specifically for Phase 2's own scope; per the SOP's cost rule ('a total-project or system figure restated on a segment row is a spec concern, not a ref'), I am not staging this as REFS_ADDED. Not disputing the number (it is plausible and arithmetically consistent), just flagging that it is unconfirmed at the phase level -- searched SEC 10-K filings (Energy Transfer Partners/Energy Transfer LP, Energy Transfer Operating LP) and FERC order text but did not locate a phase-specific capitalized-cost figure in the time available.
